name: Should I choose solid wood or MDF for interior molding?

mainEntity.name: Should I choose solid wood or MDF for interior molding?

acceptedAnswer.text: Solid wood offers distinct grain patterns, superior dent resistance, and sharp edges, making it ideal for stain-grade trim, high-traffic baseboards, and historic renovations. MDF is budget-friendly, comes pre-primed, and maintains dimensional stability without natural wood knots, making it a reliable choice for painted crown molding. However, MDF swells when exposed to standing water, making it unsuitable for wet bathroom baseboards or floor transitions. For homes in Aurora and Parker that experience seasonal humidity shifts, wood contracts and expands more noticeably at joints, whereas MDF stays relatively flat but demands careful sealing on cut ends.
acceptedAnswer.description: Choose solid wood for stain-grade finishes and high-moisture rooms, and choose MDF for painted crown molding on stable, dry walls to keep material costs down.
